title: A Miracle from the Rubble: Warsaw Old Town Walking Tour
description: A history of the Old Town’s destruction in 1944 and its rebuilding, past the reconstructed royal castle, the Jesuit church and cathedral, the main market square and the city’s brick defensive gate, ending at a lookout over the Vistula river.

title: Krakowskie Przedmieście: The fascinating story of the street
description: A history of the city’s grandest street, starting at the main entrance of the royal castle and heading south past the statue of the national poet and the old palace that now houses the university, along the old road to Kraków.

title: Warsaw at War: 1939-1945
description: A Second World War history of Warsaw from the German invasion of 1939 to the city’s destruction in 1945, passing the musical benches that play the composer Chopin’s works.

title: Łazienki Park: Legacy of the Last King
description: A walk through the royal bathhouse park laid out by Poland’s last king, Stanisław August Poniatowski, taking in the story of the warrior king who beat the Ottomans at Vienna, and the monument to the composer Chopin.

title: Wilanów Palace: Legacy of King Jan III Sobieski
description: A royal history tour of the baroque summer palace built by King Jan III Sobieski, who broke the Ottoman siege of Vienna, telling the story of his 1683 victory at the palace on the city’s southern edge.

title: From Stalin to Skyscrapers: A Walk Around Warsaw’s Palace of Culture
description: An architecture and politics walk around the Soviet-built tower Stalin gave the city in 1955, crossing the vast parade ground at its foot and ending among the glass office towers that have grown up around it since communism fell.
